H1.text: A runner on a track. A bus on a road. Your cycle on the way to college.

H2.text: Three trips. One picture can tell the whole story of each.

H3.text: Aarav rides to college. At the gate, he checks his cycle app. It shows just one line on a graph.

H4.text: His friend asks: where did you stop? Where were you fastest? Did you ever turn back?

H5.text: Aarav says one line cannot tell all that. By the end, you will read it all from the line.

P1.text: So what is a position-time graph?

P2.text: We pick a starting point, called the origin. Position x is how far you are from it. Ahead is positive.

P3.text: Time goes on the horizontal axis. Position goes on the vertical axis.

P4.text: At every moment, we mark one dot: where you are, at that time. Join the dots, and you get the x-t graph.

S1.text: Let's ride with Aarav on our motion notebook.

S2.text: Part one. He rides at a steady five metres per second. Every second, he moves the same five metres.

S3.text: Equal steps in equal times. So the graph is a straight sloping line.

S4.text: Part two. He stops at a signal. Time keeps going, but the position stays at fifty metres.

S5.text: The graph goes flat. A flat line means the object is at rest.

S6.text: Part three. He rides faster, ten metres per second. Now the line is steeper.

S7.text: Steeper line, faster motion. The steepness of the line tells you the speed.

D1.text: Let's turn steepness into a number, one step at a time.

D2.text: Step one. Pick two points on the line. Read their times and their positions.

D3.text: Step two. The change in position, delta x, is x two minus x one. The change in time, delta t, is t two minus t one.

D4.text: Step three. Slope equals delta x over delta t. That is rise over run.

D5.text: Step four. Delta x over delta t is exactly the velocity. So the slope of an x-t graph is the velocity.

T1.text: Remember this. On a position-time graph, the slope is the velocity.

K1.text: Side by side. One line goes up. The position grows, so the velocity is positive.

K2.text: The other line goes down. The position shrinks. The object is coming back towards the origin, so the velocity is negative.

K3.text: Now you try. A line slopes down. Is the object moving away from the origin, or towards it? Pause and decide.

K4.text: Towards it! A falling line means x is getting smaller, so the object moves back towards the origin. Its velocity is negative.

C1.text: Now, what if the line bends?

C2.text: Here is Aarav's ride from home. From rest, he speeds up to six metres per second in four seconds.

C3.text: Each second he covers more than the last. So the graph curves upward, getting steeper.

C4.text: At any moment, draw a tangent, a line that just touches the curve there. Its slope is the velocity at that instant.

C5.text: Then he cruises at six metres per second. A straight part. Then he brakes, and stops in three seconds, forty five metres from home.

C6.text: Your turn. In the last part, the curve gets flatter and flatter. Is he speeding up or slowing down? Pause and decide.

C7.text: Slowing down! The tangent gets less steep, until it is flat. A flat tangent means zero velocity. He has stopped.

W2.text: Aarav's position goes from fifty metres at twenty seconds to one hundred and fifty metres at thirty seconds. Find his velocity.

W3.text: Delta x is one hundred and fifty minus fifty. That is one hundred metres.

W4.text: Delta t is thirty minus twenty. That is ten seconds.

W5.text: Slope is one hundred over ten. His velocity is ten metres per second.

X2.text: Many students think an x-t graph shows the path of the object, like a hill it climbs.

X3.text: But Aarav rides on a flat, straight road. The graph is not a picture of the road. It is a record of where he was, and when.

E1.text: Where is this asked? As graph reading questions: compare the slopes of lines, or spot where the velocity is zero or negative.

Q1.text: Exam level now. Two cyclists, P and Q. On the x-t graph, P's line makes thirty degrees with the time axis, and Q's makes sixty degrees. What is the ratio of P's velocity to Q's? Pause and solve.

A1.text: The answer is B. One is to three.

A2.text: Velocity is the slope, and slope is tan of the angle with the time axis.

A3.text: Tan thirty is one over root three. Tan sixty is root three.

A4.text: So the ratio is one over root three, divided by root three. That is one third, or one is to three.

F1.text: Here is your recap. Screenshot this card.

Y1.text: Can you answer these three questions without help?

Y2.text: One. What does a flat line on an x-t graph tell you?

Y3.text: Two. How do you find the velocity from an x-t graph?

Y4.text: Three. Can an x-t graph ever be a vertical line? Why not?

N1.text: Next time: what if we plot velocity instead of position? The area under that line hides the distance. We find out in velocity-time graphs.
